title: Communications outage
tldr: Conserve phone battery, try short texts for nonurgent check-ins and use a battery radio for official information. For immediate danger, try calling local emergency services; text-to-911 availability varies. Do not travel into danger just to find signal.
steps: Try a safe available landline, another carrier or Wi-Fi calling if configured and functioning.
Send your location, status and next check-in time to your out-of-area contact.
Lower brightness, enable low-power mode and limit unnecessary use.
If networks fail completely, follow the agreed safe meeting and contact arrangements.
next: Keep paper contact lists, offline maps and a radio. Arrange check-in times before a crisis.
watch: A message sent is not necessarily delivered. Do not assume emergency texting is supported everywhere.
review_status: source-linked editorial review; not independent expert certification
without_help: Write a short message with your status, location and next check-in time; try it periodically rather than draining the battery with constant retries. Use your agreed meeting plan only when the route is safe. Do not split up to hunt for signal.
household: Give each person a written contact card and explain what to do if separated. Plan for hearing, vision, language and literacy needs. Keep live family locations and identity details off public posts even when a message seems urgent.
pack_now: Prioritize supplies named in this guide that are usable by the person who needs them. Keep the checklist and relevant contact details accessible. Check carrying capacity, storage and equipment instructions in advance; collecting equipment must not delay the immediate protective action.
faqs: Is one failed app the whole network?

Try the simplest available channel without repeated battery-draining attempts: a short text, a checked Wi-Fi connection or a prearranged contact. A local internet outage and a cellular outage may require different workarounds; do not assume every service has failed.
What if messages cannot be delivered?

Use the household’s prearranged meeting and check-in plan rather than making unplanned trips to find a signal. Keep a radio or other verified warning source if available. Record unconfirmed information separately from actual contact.
scope: Civilian educational guidance. Linked references may use U.S. emergency systems; local warning methods, laws, services and conditions differ.
sections: Choose an order such as short text, another safe connection, an out-of-area contact and an agreed meeting point. Tell everyone the expected check-in window. A failed call should not cause each person to improvise a different destination.

Keep messages brief, dim the screen where practical and close unnecessary activity. Use appropriate power banks and cables. Do not climb unsafe structures or enter danger just to obtain reception; location and accountability plans should still work without service.
